learn.hook: Who do you share your tiffin with? Who makes you laugh? That's a friend!
points: The lesson 'Best Friends' is about friendship and the fun of having a best friend.
Good friends share, help, listen and keep their promises.
Friends can disagree sometimes. They talk calmly and say sorry.
When reading, look for what the characters say and do. It shows what they are like.

example.q:
Read:
Anu and Zoya are best friends. They sit together in class. Anu is tall and loves drawing. Zoya is short and has curly hair. She tells the funniest jokes. One day, Anu forgot her lunch box. Zoya shared her poha with her. 'That is what friends are for!' said Zoya.
How did Zoya show she is a good friend?
steps: Find what happened: Anu forgot her lunch box.
Find what Zoya did: she shared her poha.
Sharing and helping are what good friends do.
example.answer: Zoya shared her poha when Anu forgot her lunch box.

learn.reallife: In school, you show friendship when you lend a pencil, share your tiffin or help a friend who has fallen down.

games.title: True or false? (about Anu and Zoya)
items: Anu and Zoya sit together in class.
The passage says 'They sit together in class.'
It was Anu who forgot her lunch box.
Zoya shared her poha with Anu.
The passage says 'Zoya shared her poha with her.'
Good friends laugh when you fall down.
Good friends help you get up.
Friends can say sorry after a fight.
Saying sorry helps friends make up.

games.title: Match the friendship word
pairs: give some of what you have
say you will surely do something
what we say when we make a mistake

quiz.q: The passage begins: 'Anu and Zoya are best friends.' Who are the best friends?
quiz.explain: The first line names Anu and Zoya as best friends.
quiz.mistake: Did not read the first line

quiz.q: 'Anu and Zoya are best friends. They sit together in class.' Where do they sit together?
quiz.explain: The line says they sit together in class.
quiz.mistake: Guessed a place instead of reading the line

quiz.q: 'Anu is tall and loves drawing.' What does Anu love?
quiz.explain: The line says Anu loves drawing.
quiz.mistake: Picked a hobby without reading the line

quiz.q: 'One day, Anu forgot her lunch box.' What did Anu forget?
quiz.explain: The line tells us Anu forgot her lunch box.
quiz.mistake: Did not find the line about forgetting

quiz.q: 'Zoya shared her poha with her.' What did Zoya share?
quiz.explain: Zoya shared her poha, which was in her lunch box.
quiz.mistake: Guessed a food without reading

quiz.q: Zoya shares her food and says, 'That is what friends are for!' What does she mean?
quiz.explain: Zoya means friends help each other when they need it.
quiz.mistake: Did not think about why Zoya said it

quiz.q: Which is a good thing for a friend to do?
quiz.explain: Good friends share and help. The others are unkind.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that laughing at someone or breaking promises is unkind

quiz.q: Two friends want to play different games. What is a good thing to do?
quiz.explain: Talking calmly and taking turns keeps friends happy.
quiz.mistake: Thinks shouting or pushing solves a problem

teach.ask: Gappu wants a best friend. He asks: 'What does a good friend do?'
teach.praise: I will share my seeds with my friends! Thank you!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me two things a good friend does?

learn.hook: Can you describe your best friend so well that I could find them in a crowd?
points: Describing words tell us more about a person, animal, place or thing.
Some describing words tell how a friend looks: tall, short, curly hair, big eyes.
Some tell what a friend is like: kind, funny, honest, brave, helpful, cheerful.
Many describing words have opposites: tall – short, happy – sad.

example.q: Describe Zoya in one sentence. Clues: she is short, has curly hair and tells funny jokes.
steps: Pick a word for how she looks: short, curly hair.
Pick a word for what she is like: funny.
Put them together in a sentence.
example.answer: Zoya is a short, funny girl with curly hair.

learn.reallife: When you write a birthday card or tell your family about a new classmate, you use describing words.

quiz.q: In 'Zoya has curly hair', which word describes the hair?
quiz.explain: 'curly' tells us what Zoya's hair is like.
quiz.mistake: Picks the naming word instead of the describing word

quiz.q: Which is a describing word?
quiz.explain: 'cheerful' describes a happy person. 'run' is an action word, and 'school' and 'pencil' are naming words.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up describing words with naming or action words

quiz.q: 'My friend Neha always tells the truth.' Which word describes Neha?
quiz.explain: A person who tells the truth is honest.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'honest'

quiz.q: 'Kartik makes everyone laugh.' Which word describes Kartik?
quiz.explain: Someone who makes people laugh is funny.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that does not match what Kartik does

quiz.q: 'Pooja is not afraid of the dark.' Which word describes Pooja?
quiz.explain: Someone who is not afraid is brave.
quiz.mistake: Picks the opposite of brave

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'tall'?
quiz.explain: The opposite of tall is short.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that means almost the same as tall

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'happy'?
quiz.explain: The opposite of happy is sad. 'Glad' and 'cheerful' mean almost the same as happy.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with a similar meaning instead of the opposite

quiz.q: Which sentence tells how a friend looks?
quiz.explain: 'long black hair' describes Sam's looks. The others tell what Sam is like or does.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up looks with nature or actions

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I describe my friend Chiku the squirrel?'
teach.praise: Chiku is small, brown, funny and kind! I described him!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me words for how a friend looks and what a friend is like?

learn.hook: 'Anu is tall. Anu loves drawing. Anu has a red bag.' Too many Anus! How can we fix it?
points: A pronoun is a word used in place of a naming word.
Use 'he' for a boy or man, and 'she' for a girl or woman.
Use 'it' for a thing, and 'they' for more than one person or thing.
Use 'we' when you talk about yourself and others together.
Pronouns stop us from saying the same name again and again.

example.q: Make this better: 'Kartik is my friend. Kartik plays cricket.'
example.answer: Kartik is my friend. He plays cricket.

learn.reallife: When you talk about your family at dinner, you say 'she' for Didi and 'he' for Bhaiya without even thinking!

games.title: Match the naming word to its pronoun

items.text: Dadi is in the garden. ___ is watering the tulsi plant.
My bag is new. ___ is blue.
Arjun and Sana are playing. ___ are happy.
Papa is cooking. ___ is making dal.

quiz.q: 'Zoya is my friend. ___ tells funny jokes.' Which word fits?
quiz.explain: Zoya is a girl, so we use 'she'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'he' for a girl

quiz.q: 'Rahul is tall. ___ plays basketball.' Which word fits?
quiz.explain: Rahul is a boy, so we use 'he'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'she' or 'it' for a boy

quiz.q: 'Anu and Zoya are friends. ___ sit together.' Which word fits?
quiz.explain: Anu and Zoya are two people, so we use 'they'.
quiz.mistake: Uses a pronoun for one person when there are two

quiz.q: 'Look at the kite! ___ is flying high.' Which word fits?
quiz.explain: A kite is a thing, so we use 'it'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'he' or 'she' for a thing

quiz.q: 'Raju and I went to the park. ___ played on the swings.' Which word fits?
quiz.explain: 'Raju and I' includes me, so we use 'we'.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that 'I' is part of the group

quiz.q: Which pronoun can take the place of 'the ball'?
quiz.explain: A ball is a thing, so we use 'it'.
quiz.mistake: Thinks things can be called he or she

quiz.q: Which of these is a pronoun?
quiz.explain: 'they' is used in place of naming words. The others are a noun, an action word and a colour word.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a pronoun is

quiz.q: Why do we use pronouns?
options: so we do not repeat the same name again and again
quiz.explain: Pronouns take the place of names so our sentences sound better.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up pronouns with describing or action words

teach.ask: Gappu says: 'Gappu is hungry. Gappu wants seeds. Gappu is tired.' Then he asks: 'How can I stop saying Gappu so much?'
teach.praise: I am hungry. I want seeds. I am tired. Much better!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me which words we use in place of names, like 'he' and 'she'?
